page: Microsoft Azure F64-16ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading enabled, resulting in one thread per core. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, translating to a high resource density of 32.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the F64-16ams_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core metrics. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also rank in the top tier. Multi-core and multi-threaded performance, including Geekbench multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, ranges from average to strong. Memory performance is robust, with PassMark memory scores in the top 25% and average uncached read and write memory bandwidth.

Given its massive memory allocation of 512.0 GB relative to 16 vCPUs, this server is highly optimized for memory-intensive workloads. It is well-suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and data-intensive processing tasks. The high single-core clock speed of 4.5 GHz also makes it effective for single-threaded execution paths and low-latency text or image processing. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, which should be factored into architectural designs.
